title: AIDA design guides-read record
description: Which guide bodies design opened, at <task folder>/design-guides-read.json, beside design-closed.json and never inside design/ (ideal/design.md, 'What design reads'). Research names guides without opening them, so design is the first read, and nothing else records what it read. A second design run in a new session compares each entry's sha256 to the body on disk and reads only what changed and what is not recorded (live-run row 77). It sits at the task's own root because every design/*.json is read as a work order, by the check and by the closed hash, and a re-read must not move that hash. Written by design-actions.sh read-guide, one entry per path, a second read of the same path replacing its entry. check-design.sh reads it only to refuse a malformed one. A field present in a real record but absent from this schema's `properties` is a defect in the schema, not a value to silently accept, which is why `additionalProperties` is false.

schemaVersion.description: The shape this file was written in, the same field design-closed.json and every design/*.json carry. Bumped only when a later change to this schema says so, never for a value change inside an unchanged shape.

guides.description: One entry per guide body design opened, keyed by path. Empty is a real state: design started and opened nothing yet.

path.description: The body on disk, as an absolute path: what the navigator's lookup returned, or a project's own source file. The key a second read-guide replaces on.

sha256.description: sha256 over the body's bytes at the moment it was read, computed by the script and never typed by hand. A resumed `start` re-derives it and prints `changed` when the two differ, or `missing` when no readable file is at the path.

readAt.description: The UTC date the body was read, YYYY-MM-DD, set by the script.

name.description: The name research gave this guide in its own finding, when read-guide was passed --name. A later read-guide on the same path without --name keeps it. Absent otherwise. It joins the body read here to the finding that named it.
